rule: These numbers are not changed after a comparison has run. A failure is investigated and reported; a tolerance is never widened.
numbers_from: DLC/tests/fald_fade_frozen_tolerances.json, sha256 (LF) 9267ba793571f4f1da0eb35986f7ca7ac11a423ee02817c9365bbcc051f1fb25 — its gate1_f32_vs_f64 and gate2_hlsl_vs_f32 blocks, unchanged; the gate tests read the numbers from it and check both files' hashes
off_gate: unchanged: bit for bit against tests/fixtures/fald_fade_off_main.hashes
gate1_f32_vs_f64: as fald_fade_frozen_tolerances.json gate1_f32_vs_f64 (fields 2e-4 abs incl. fade, fade_T, s, reach_r0/1; lit 2e-4 abs, F 2e-4 rel; out16 >= 99.9 % within 2 FP16 steps, max 8; cut / shift as before), the twin = r12a/cands12a.py F12A_B16, the study logs = r12a/out/motion12a F12A_B16
gate2_hlsl_vs_f32: as fald_fade_frozen_tolerances.json gate2_hlsl_vs_f32 (out16 <= 1 step; base fields rtol 1e-6 / atol 2e-5; fade fields rtol 1e-6 / atol 5e-5; F rel 1e-5; flags array_equal; shift 1e-3 texel)
note: the padded closing and the sigma-16 floor Gaussian are inside the compared fields (fade / fade_T, lit, F); no new field, no new tolerance. B16's Gaussian is the same Kahan kernel as sigma 24 / 32 (129 taps < 193 / 257), so atol 5e-5 on lit and F rel 1e-5 are stated without a pre-run.
cells: the current set + aces_m18, aces_m52, s10_ac_redspot

negative_control.rule: a deliberate one-constant mutation must FAIL the gate it belongs to; the code is restored and the gate passes again
mutations: A: the closing's zero padding 80 -> 40 texels (fadeemu CL_PAD for gate 1; HLSL FADE_CL_PAD + the C++ pad for gate 2)
B16: the lit-floor Gaussian sigma 16 -> 12 (fadeemu OF_FLOOR_SIG for gate 1; the C++ Gauss call for gate 2)
